---
title: "check-literal-math-letters.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, warn-only check that flags literal Latin and Greek letters in math
where a semantic macro from
[`Morrison-Lab/macros`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/macros) belongs.
The lab's rule is that every math symbol is a semantic macro
(`\outvar`, `\predvar`, `\param`, ...),
so no literal letter appears in math
outside a passage about the notation itself,
except a one-off with no semantic category.
This is check 1 of
[gha#1077](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1077).

The check flags, inside inline (`$...$`) and display (`$$...$$`,
`\begin{equation}`, `\begin{align}`, and the like) math:

- **A standalone single Latin letter.**
  A run of exactly one ASCII letter that is not part of a `\command` name,
  such as the `y` in `$y_i$`.
- **Any Greek command or character.**
  `\alpha` through `\omega`, `\varepsilon`, `\varphi`, the capitals,
  and a literal Greek character such as the Greek small theta.

Each finding names the letters on the line.
Where the macro library has a macro for the letter,
the message suggests it:
`y` for `\outvar`, `Y` for `\Outvar`, `x` for `\predvar`, `X` for `\Predvar`,
`n` for `\nobs`, `L` for `\loss`,
`\theta` for `\param`, `\beta` for `\regcoef`,
`\varepsilon` for `\eps` and `\mu` for `\mean`.
These suggestions are conditional ("if this is the outcome variable"),
since a letter alone does not say what it names.

The check does not flag:

- the argument of a text-like command:
  `\text{}`, `\textrm{}`, `\mathrm{}`, `\operatorname{}`, `\mbox{}`,
  and reference-like commands such as `\label{}`, `\tag{}`, `\eqref{}`,
  `\begin{}` and `\end{}`;
- `\mathbb{...}`, whose letters name standard sets and operators
  (`ai-config`'s `check-raw-math.py` covers those);
- a run of two or more letters, such as `df`;
- code fences, inline code spans, HTML comments and YAML front matter;
- any `::: {.notation}` div (also written `::: notation`),
  a passage that discusses the notation itself,
  including a div nested inside it;
- a math span that defines a macro
  (`\newcommand`, `\renewcommand`, `\providecommand`, `\def`,
  `\DeclareMathOperator`), which is check 2 of the issue;
- a line carrying, or following, `<!-- check-literal-math-letters: allow -->`,
  or a file carrying `<!-- check-literal-math-letters: ignore-file -->`.

The check is strict:
there is no allow-list for indices or dummy variables.
The rule says to find the category first,
so the check starts strict and the false-positive rate is measured
(see below) before anyone decides to relax it.

## Scope

Only lines a pull request adds are reported,
so a corpus that already carries literal letters is not reflagged
on every unrelated edit.
The whole file is parsed, because a display block opens on one line
and its letters sit on a later one,
and only findings on added lines are kept.
An added line whose exact text was also deleted in the same diff
counts as moved rather than new.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed
(a shallow clone, an unresolvable ref),
the check skips with a warning.
It never falls back to a whole-tree scan,
which would reflag every existing letter.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked file in full on purpose.

Every run prints how many lines, files and math spans it examined,
so a run that examined nothing reads differently
from one that examined everything and found nothing.

## Limitations

- Inline math that spans a line break is not recognized.
  A `$...$` pair must open and close on one source line,
  which semantic line breaks normally preserve.
- A brand new untracked file is invisible to `git diff`.
  Stage it to have a local run examine it.
- A run of two or more letters (`xy`) is not a single letter and is not flagged.
- A passage about the notation must be in a `.notation` div to be exempt.
  A heading titled "Notation" is not enough.

## False-positive rate

Measured on 2026-10-16 in whole-tree mode over `chapters/*.qmd`:

| Repository | Files | Math spans | Lines flagged |
| ---------- | ----: | ---------: | ------------: |
| `psw`      |    37 |        376 | 242 of 5,624 lines (4.3%) |
| `lds`      | 1,658 |     15,856 | 7,312 of 78,669 lines (9.3%) |

A random sample of 65 flagged lines across the two repositories
held no hit outside math,
so the parser's own error rate is low.
Whether a literal index letter is a false positive
is a policy question for the maintainers:
lines whose only letters are the common index letters `i j k l m n t`
are 5% of the `psw` hits and 11% of the `lds` hits,
so an allow-list for indices would remove little of the volume.

## Inputs

| Input          | Type    | Default               | Description |
| -------------- | ------- | --------------------- | ----------- |
| `globs`        | string  | `'*.qmd *.md *.Rmd'`  | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore` | string  | `''`                  | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`         | boolean | `false`               | Fail the workflow when a literal letter is found. Warn-only by default. |
| `whole-tree`   | boolean | `false`               | Scan every tracked file in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string | `'3.x'`              | Python version to set up. |
| `mode` | string | `'all'` | `all` flags every standalone letter. `known` flags only a letter or Greek command that has a semantic macro (`y`, `Y`, `x`, `X`, `n`, `L`, `e`, `\theta`, `\beta`, `\varepsilon`, `\mu`), so index letters pass. |
| `deprecated-files` | string | `''` | Space-separated interpretation files (for example `latex-macros/interpretations.tsv`). A row saying `deprecated, use \x` marks that macro deprecated, and a use on an added line is flagged. |
| `submodules` | string | `'false'` | Passed to `actions/checkout`, so a macros submodule is available for `deprecated-files`. |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-literal-math-letters.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags literal Latin and Greek letters in math (a bare `y`,
# `\theta`) on lines a PR adds, where a semantic macro from Morrison-Lab/macros
# (`\outvar`, `\predvar`, `\param`) belongs. Warn-only by default; skips code,
# comments, `\text{}`-like commands and any `::: {.notation}` div.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check literal letters in math

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-literal-math-letters.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd *.md *.Rmd'              # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'   # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: true                             # block instead of warn (defaults to false)
    #   whole-tree: true                       # scan every line, not just a PR's additions
```

See
[`examples/check-literal-math-letters.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-literal-math-letters.yml)
for the full caller stub.
